findings.title: On ticket_link questions the "ticket" filter drops key-only linked tickets, which makes a plan answering with the ticket's key valid. That is the cause of the retest loss.
findings.evidence:
Every ticket_link wording says "ticket", and the start is a Linear or Jira item. So own_systems already contains "ticket", and target_system falls back to systems[0]="ticket" (line 262). candidates() then puts [ticket] on every plan that reaches a tracker item (line 285), and execute/ends filter with in_system(e, "ticket") (line 339).

in_system uses system_of_entity. That returns "" for 'identifier' entities, which are ticket keys with no document in the bank, such as key:eng-27184. The filter therefore removes them from the plan's end set.

This matters on mdfresh ticket_link-assignee-028, "ENG-421987 is connected to another ticket. Whose name is on that one?":
- dependencies = [key:eng-27184 (identifier, system ''), ENG-33456 (linear)].
- With tickets off, the plan 'dependencies -> label -> single' is not a candidate, because the two keys disagree. The plan reading the asked field wins (Liam Chen, correct).
- With tickets on, the filter leaves one entity, so 'dependencies [ticket] -> label -> single' => ENG-33456 becomes a valid candidate. The asked kind is not sure (None), so check 4 does not remove it, and it scores 0.823 against 0.817 for the assignee plan.

The rule creates this candidate, not the reweighting:
- With v9's weights and tickets=True, it scores 0.902 against 0.975. The answer is still right, but the plan was absent before.
- With v9's weights and tickets=True, mdblind ticket_link-assignee-019 and mdplan_w1 ticket_link-status-025 also switch to answering with a ticket key.
- With v11's weights, tickets off versus on gives the same three changes plus mdwords ticket_link-status-024.

Exposure is wide. Most ticket_link starts link to identifiers as well as the one ticket document: 11 in mdtrain, 9 in mdtest, 8 in mdfresh, 7 in mdwords, 6 in mdblind, 7 in mdllm, 7 in mdplan and 3 in mdrep. The same applies to PRs whose linked_linear includes keys with no document.

v12 avoided this loss in development only because the form supplies the kind.
findings.fix: Count ticket keys with no document as members of "ticket". For example, in_system(e, "ticket") could also accept an identifier entity whose label matches the tracker key pattern, so the filter cannot shrink an ambiguous set of linked keys to one. Alternatively, when tickets is on and the target is "ticket" while "ticket" is already one of the start's own systems, do not set sys_f, because the question then names no system other than the start's own. Either change keeps v9 unchanged. The pre-registration should name the rule, not the reweighting, as the cause of the retest loss.

verdict.reason:
I reproduced the finding and could not refute it. I changed no repo files; my check scripts are in the scratchpad (chk_tl.py, chk_all.py).

**The mechanism.** In mdfresh ticket_link-assignee-028, the start doc:dsid_77f0… (Linear) has dependencies = [key:eng-27184 (an identifier; system_of_entity returns ''), ENG-33456 (Linear)]. systems_named returns ['ticket'] and own_systems returns {linear, ticket}. target_system therefore falls back to systems[0] = 'ticket'. candidates() sets sys_f = 'ticket', and execute/ends filter with in_system(e, 'ticket'), which drops the identifier.

**What changes, by lessons and switch:**
- v9 lessons, tickets off: no 'dependencies → label → single' candidate, because the two keys disagree. Liam Chen wins at 0.798.
- v9 lessons, tickets on: the candidate appears ('dependencies [ticket] → label → single' gives ENG-33456 at 0.902). The assignee plan still wins at 0.975.
- v11 lessons, tickets off: Liam Chen (correct), and the label plan is again absent.
- v11 lessons, tickets on: ENG-33456 at 0.823 beats Liam Chen at 0.817. Score 0.

So the switch creates the wrong candidate, and the new weights let it win. With v11's lessons and the switch off, the answer is right.

**The other cited cases (all confirmed):**
- With v9 lessons and the switch on, mdblind ticket_link-assignee-019 and mdplan_w1 ticket_link-status-025 also switch to a ticket key.
- With v11 lessons, off versus on gives those same changes plus mdwords ticket_link-status-024 (Benji Okafor to Amara Diallo, both wrong).

**The suggested fix, tried as an in-memory patch.** I made in_system(e, 'ticket') also accept identifier entities whose label is a tracker key, and ran v11 (switch on) over all 15 dev sets:
- mdfresh ticket_link-assignee-028 goes from 0 to 1 (Liam Chen).
- mdblind ticket_link-assignee-019 goes from 0 to 1 (Priya Kapoor).
- mdplan_w1 ticket_link-status-025 changes from one wrong answer to another.
- Nothing else changes. The action-item gains are intact.

**One correction.** The pre-registration draft does not actually blame the reweighting for the loss. It lists 'One loss' with no cause given, so that part of the suggested fix is only about wording. The core defect is concrete.

**Why it matters for the test.** The same filter applies to any ticket-worded question that starts from a Linear/Jira item or a pull request whose links include keys with no document. That covers ticket_link and pr_issue questions, and most starts have such keys (6 to 11 per set, per the reviewer). The test's brief told writers to say 'ticket' and not name a tracker, so v11 will apply this filter far more often on the test than in development. On Linear-worded dev questions, v9 already filtered on 'linear', so both arms behaved alike. On the test, v9 does not filter and v11 does.

Each such loss counts against rule 2 (v11 ≥ v9 − 0.03 per question on the other questions). That is the rule that decides whether the ticket rule works. It also lowers v11/v12 test numbers wherever the form gives no kind. Fixing this before freezing would likely change test numbers and could change the rule 2 verdict.

findings.title: Any "ticket" or "issue" in a question that starts outside Linear and Jira forces the answer from Linear or Jira, even when the question asks about the start itself
findings.evidence:
systems_named appends "ticket" whenever TICKET_WORD matches anywhere in the question. target_system returns the first named system that is not one of the start's own. For a GitHub or meeting start, that is "ticket" even when the question asks about the start. Check 2 then keeps only plans with p.system == "ticket".

Target system, v9 then v11:
- "the GitHub issue for it" from a GitHub start: github, then ticket.
- "the pull request for the ticket" from a GitHub start: github, then ticket.
- "the issue in the meeting" or "re-issue the meeting notes" from a meeting start: fireflies, then ticket.

Effect on mdrep, "Who authored pull request #20357, the one that fixes the login issue?":
- v9 answers Priya Singh (the author, correct).
- v11 answers Marco Diaz, via 'linked_linear [ticket] -> assignee'.
- "PR #20357 closes a ticket. Who authored the PR?" changes the same way.

Systematic probe on mdtrain, mdtest, mdfresh, mdplan, mdrep and mdblind, over every PR with a linked Linear issue: "Who authored pull request #N, which is linked to a ticket?" and "... It fixes an issue." v9 gets 82 of 88 right. v9's weights with tickets=True lose 74 of those 82, and the v11 lessons lose 37 of 41 on the first wording.

None of the seven test kinds starts at a PR or a meeting and asks about it, so the pre-registered test does not exercise this. Note that v9 already behaves this way when a tracker is named by name ("...linked to a Linear issue"). v11 extends the behaviour to the bare words, which are far more common.
findings.fix: Let "ticket" become the target only when the ticket word is plausibly what is asked about, not merely mentioned. One option is to add "ticket" only when no other system is named, or when the start's own system is the only other one named and the start is not itself what the question's main noun refers to. A simpler guard: when the start's own system is named explicitly ("pull request", "PR", "meeting", "GitHub"), keep v9's target and use "ticket" only as a tie-breaker, not as a hard check-2 target. At minimum, document the limitation in the pre-registration and the results.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. The finding is correct.

Code path (cie/src/cie/factbank/plans.py):
- `systems_named` (lines 330-337) appends "ticket" whenever `TICKET_WORD` matches anywhere in the question.
- `target_system` (lines 323-328) returns the first named system that is not one of the start's own.
- `own_systems` (lines 344-347) adds "ticket" only for a Linear or Jira start.

So for a GitHub start, a question that names both "pull request" and "ticket" targets "ticket". Check 2 (`other_system`, lines 371-374) then keeps only plans with `p.system == "ticket"`.

Reproduced on mdrep with the frozen fb50 lessons and the mdtrain `plan_lessons_v9.json` / `plan_lessons_v11.json`:
- "Who authored pull request #20357, the one that fixes the login issue?"
  - v9: Priya Singh, via `[github] → author`.
  - v11: Marco Diaz, via `→ linked_linear [ticket] → assignee`.
- "PR #20357 closes a ticket. Who authored the PR?" flips the same way.
- "Who authored pull request #20357?" is unchanged.

Systematic probe over every PR with a `linked_linear` link in mdrep, mdtest and mdplan (24 PRs):

| wording | v9 | v11 |
|---|---|---|
| "Who authored pull request #N, which is linked to a ticket?" | 21/24 | 0/24 |
| "Who authored pull request #N? It fixes an issue." | 21/24 | 0/24 |
| "...linked to a Linear issue?" | 0/24 | 0/24 |
| plain "Who authored pull request #N?" | 21/24 | 21/24 |

This confirms the finding's note that v9 already fails when the tracker is named. v11 extends that failure to the bare words "ticket" and "issue".

Effect on the test: none on its numbers or verdict. All seven kinds (pr_issue, issue_pr_author, ticket_link, person_count, person_first, compare_two, action_owner_issues) behave as intended under v11, and none starts at a PR or a meeting and asks about that start:
- pr_issue starts at a PR and asks about the linked ticket, so "ticket" is the right target.
- issue_pr_author starts at a Linear item, which is already in "ticket", so the target stays github.
- action_owner_issues starts at a meeting and asks about tickets, which is the intended fix.

So rule 2 ("no harm on the other questions") and the development sets cannot see this regression. The pre-registration (cie/docs/FACTBANK_TICKET_PREREGISTRATION.md) does not mention it. Noting it there or in the results write-up is a documentation matter and would not change any number.

findings.title: Rule 1/3 are scored on all action-item questions, but nothing defines or counts the ones that 'name no tracker', so the verdict depends on how the wordings were drawn
findings.evidence: ticket_test (around line 774) sets `action = {"action_owner_issues"}` and `share()` averages own_score over every question of that kind. That matches the literal text of rules 1 and 3 ('on the test set's action-item questions'). The rule's own title, 'when no tracker is named', and the pre-registration's promise to report 'how many of the test's action-item questions name no tracker' are not backed by any code: neither ticket_test nor run_ticket.sh decides whether a question names a tracker or counts such questions. Development shows that this split, not the ticket rule, decides the verdict. I recomputed from dev_v9/v11/v10/v12 rows. On the as-drawn sets, whose wordings named Linear, v9's action-item share is already 0.938 (mdplan) and 1.0 (mdrep), so v11 - v9 can be at most 0.062 or 0. Only on the plain-words writer runs is v9 low enough: 0.5 (mdplan_w3) and 0.667 (mdrep_w3), against v11 0.938 and 1.0. Rule 1 needs v9 <= 0.75 even if v11 is perfect. If roughly half the drawn action-item wordings name a tracker, v9 is about 0.75 to 0.83 and rule 1 fails while the ticket rule works. I ran ticket_test end to end on stand-ins (test=mdplan, changed=mdrep, training=mdtrain, training_all=mdtrainv9, earlier = the 7 sets), with v11/v12 answers produced by the CLI `ask` path. It gave rules 1 and 3 'not met' (0.938 vs 0.938) and rules 2 and 4 to 7 'met'. That run also shows the code itself works. Without a definition fixed now, the promised count would be computed after the wordings are seen, with a criterion chosen then.
findings.fix: Before unsealing, add a frozen definition to ticket_test. One option: a question names a tracker if `Planner.systems_named` with tickets=False returns 'linear' or 'jira'; the SYSTEM_WORDS check works too. Report n_action, n_action_no_tracker and the v9/v11/v10/v12 shares on that subset in ticket_report.json. In the pre-registration, say whether rules 1 and 3 are judged on all action items (as now) or on the no-tracker subset, and what the verdict is if that subset is empty or has fewer than about 3 questions (e.g. 'not measurable' rather than 'not met').

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every factual claim in the finding holds.

**The code**
- `ticket_test` (cie/src/cie/eval/factbank_multi.py:770-786) scores rules 1 and 3 with `share()` over every question whose kind is `action_owner_issues`.
- No code decides whether a question names a tracker, and none counts such questions. I checked `ticket_test`, `run_ticket.sh` (identical to the scratchpad copy) and `single_writers.py`.
- The pre-registration still promises that "How many of the test's action-item questions name no tracker will be reported", and says "Rules 1 and 2 decide whether the ticket rule works". It does not say what the verdict is when few questions name no tracker.

**Why the mix decides the verdict**
- In `questions()`, each action-item question draws its wording at random from the pair of templates (writer 1 and writer 2).
- So the test set has 0%, about 50%, or 100% of its roughly 8 or 9 action items naming a tracker. That depends only on whether each writer's single template says Linear or Jira.

**Development numbers, recomputed from the dev_v9/v11/v10/v12 rows**
- Every as-drawn set and the w1/w2 sets name "linear" in all their action items. On these, v9 already scores 0.938 to 1.0, and v11 − v9 is at most 0.062. It is 0 on mdplan (0.938 vs 0.938) and on mdrep (1.0 vs 1.0).
- Only the plain-words writer names no tracker (mdplan_w3: 0 of 8 named; mdrep_w3: 0 of 9). There v9 scores 0.5 and 0.667, and v11 scores 0.938 and 1.0.
- No quoted meeting title or action-item text in any set contained "linear" or "jira".
- From these numbers, v11 − v9 is roughly 0.39f + 0.03(1−f), where f is the share of action items that name no tracker. That passes +0.25 only if f is about 0.6 or more.
- So if one of the two drawn templates names Linear (f about 0.5), rule 1 and likewise rule 3 would likely come out "not met" even if the ticket rule works perfectly. Under the frozen text, that reads as "the ticket rule does not work".

**The promised count has no fixed definition**
- The count would be defined only after the wordings are seen. There are real choices to make:
  - whether it is judged on the template or on the filled question (a meeting title like "nonlinear ..." would trip a substring check);
  - whether a generic "tracker" counts as naming one.

**Tests**
- tests/test_factbank_multi.py passes (17 passed). So this is a gap in the design and reporting, not a code crash.

**Fix, before unsealing**
- Freeze the criterion. Judging it on the `action_owner_issues` templates in wordings.json, by whether they contain "linear" or "jira", is cleaner than running `systems_named` on the filled questions.
- Report n_action, n_no_tracker and each arm's share on that subset in ticket_report.json.
- State in the pre-registration whether rules 1 and 3 are judged on all action items or on the no-tracker subset, and that the verdict is "not measurable" if the subset is too small.

findings.title: The Jira check and other promised reports are not computed by the frozen script
findings.evidence:
The pre-registration says the check that people asked about have no Jira tickets 'will be checked again on the test set and reported'. It also lists 'whether any person asked about has Jira tickets', 'the same questions in each writer's wording' and 'v12's form use and the model's time' under 'Also reported'. ticket_test computes none of them. run_ticket.sh answers mdtick_w1..w3 with every arm but never measures them. The Jira check affects scores. questions() builds expected keys only from `source == "linear"` documents, while units() can pull Jira→Jira 'ticket' units into the 50 documents. If an action-item owner also holds a Jira ticket there, v11's 'ticket' system adds that key and is scored below 1 by F1. I checked the earlier-set claim and it holds: Jira documents appear in mdtrain (6), mdfresh (2) and mdblind (2), but none of their assignees holds a Linear issue in the same set. So the check matters only for the new draw.

Everything else in this lens checked out:
- All 7 rules match the pre-registration in thresholds, signs, sets and arms: per-question shares for rules 1 to 3 (consistent with how earlier results used 'share right'), three-group means for rules 4 to 7, training_all = mdtrainv9 for rule 5, mdtrain v4 for rule 7, and the 7 as-drawn sets for rule 4.
- run_ticket.sh writes every file ticket_test reads (v4/8/9/10/11/12 on mdtick and mdtickchanged; v11/v12 on mdtrain, mdtrainv9 and the 7 earlier sets).
- Lesson hashes match the frozen ones (v11 24fd4751, v9 00e63e5f, v4 74715075, v8 ad549716). v9 has no 'tickets' field.
- Stored v9/v10 answers on all 15 earlier folders equal the dev reruns under the new code, 0 differing answers. CLI v11/v12 answers equal the dev rows on all 9 sets, 0 differing.
- The exclude list covers every haystack.json in the scratchpad (42 files, 0 documents outside the excluded union).
- In the single-writer step, only the path changed. Its question seed 44 = 43+1 matches build_fresh. Its random draws stay in step with the drawn pairs because choice() from 1 or 2 options uses the same number of random draws. Its writer-file format could not be checked without opening blind4.
- The tests pass (21).
findings.fix: Add to ticket_test, before unsealing, the parts that need no answers. (a) For each test question, whether the person asked about (pieces[0] for action items, the named person for person_count/person_first) is the assignee of any Jira document in mdtick's haystack. (b) A measure() of each mdtick_w{i} folder: three-group mean and action/other shares per arm. (c) v12's form use and model_ms, taken from the factbank_v12 rows or the form cache. Save all of them in ticket_report.json so they come from frozen code.

verdict.reason:
The finding's factual claim holds, but nothing that decides the test depends on it.

What holds:
- `ticket_test` (cie/src/cie/eval/factbank_multi.py:762-802) computes only `measure()` for training, training_all, held_out and changed, the action/other shares, the earlier-set means and the 7 rules.
- It does not compute the Jira check, the per-writer scores, v12's form use or model time. It also does not count the action-item questions that name no tracker, which the pre-registration also promises.
- run_ticket.sh answers mdtick_w1..w3, but its last command does not pass them to `ticket`.
- The design point is also real. `questions()` builds `expected.ids` only from `source=="linear"` documents. `units()` can bring Jira→Jira ticket units into the 50 documents. `TICKET_SYSTEMS={"linear","jira"}` lets v11 and v12 include a Jira key. The pre-registration already says this ("'tickets' could rightly include Jira tickets, while the test's expected answers count only Linear issues").

Why it does not matter for the test:
1. **No rule uses these items.** Rules 1-7 are computed entirely by frozen code. The items are listed as "Also reported", meaning information only.
2. **Every input is saved by frozen code, so the items can be worked out exactly after the run.**
   - `ask_plans` writes each arm's answers for mdtick_w1..w3.
   - Each factbank_v12 row stores `form`, including `model_ms` from `Former` (reader.py:208), and `learned_kind`.
   - The Jira check is a fixed property of mdtick's haystack.json and questions.jsonl (`pieces[0]` is the owner). It needs no answers and leaves almost no analytic freedom.
3. **This matches the earlier tests.** Both earlier pre-registrations (FACTBANK_PLAN_PREREGISTRATION.md and FACTBANK_PLAN_REPLICATION.md) listed the same kind of items under "Also reported": single-writer scores, form use, model time. Their frozen `plan_test` did not compute them either. They were produced afterwards from the stored rows (docs/benchmarks/factbank_plan/replication/summary.json holds model_ms_median, form_differs and the _w1.._w3 sets).
4. **The Jira effect works against the new arms.** If an owner holds a Jira ticket in mdtick, only v11 and v12 can lose points, so rules 1 and 3 could only become harder to meet. Computing the check inside `ticket_test` would change no score and no verdict. It would only explain a score.

Tests pass (21).

Adding (a)-(c) to `ticket_test` would be a useful convenience, so these reports come from frozen code. It is not needed for the test's numbers, verdicts or fairness.

findings.title: Rule 1 mostly measures whether the writers named a tracker, not whether the ticket rule works, and the pre-registration says nothing about what happens if few questions name none
findings.evidence:
How the test is built: questions() picks each question's wording with rng.choice from the pair (writer 1's and writer 2's template). So the test's 8-9 action-item questions are just 2 templates filled with different meetings and tasks. On mdplan and mdrep both drawn templates said "Linear".

What development shows (recomputed from dev_*.json):
- On every set whose action template names Linear (mdtest, mdfresh, mdwords, mdllm, mdplan, mdrep, mdplan_w1/w2, mdrep_w1/w2), v11-v9 on action items is 0.000.
- The whole gain comes from writer 3's single template: mdplan_w3 +0.438 and mdrep_w3 +0.333.
- Even there, v9 already got 10 of the 17 tracker-free questions right. So a tracker-free question gives a gain only about 41% of the time.

The threshold arithmetic:
- +0.25 needs a net 2 of 8 questions, or 2.25 of 9 (2/9 = 0.222 fails).
- If exactly one of the two templates names no tracker (about 4 questions), the expected gain is about 1.7 questions, or about 0.2. A perfectly working rule would then probably fail.
- If both templates name a tracker, the rule cannot pass at all.
- The questions also cluster on a few owners (mdtest: 9 action questions on 2 owners; mdtrain: 8 on 4), so the effective sample is smaller still.

The label does not match the code. Rule 1 is labelled "when no tracker is named", but ticket_test computes it over every action_owner_issues row.

The pre-registration only promises to report how many questions name no tracker. It does not say what that count changes. 'Rules 1 and 2 decide' then invites interpretation after the fact.
findings.fix:
Before freezing:
- Define "names no tracker" mechanically, e.g. the question contains neither "linear" nor "jira", ignoring case.
- Compute rules 1 and 3 on that subset.
- Pre-declare that below N such questions (e.g. 4), rule 1 is reported as 'not measurable' rather than as a pass or fail.
- Alternatively, set the threshold against the room for improvement, e.g. v11 is right on at least X% of the tracker-free action questions that v9 gets wrong.
- Consider giving rules to the single-writer runs (mdtick_w1..w3), which the run script already produces, since each writer's template is the real unit being tested.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not; every concrete claim checks out.

Code:
- ticket_test (cie/src/cie/eval/factbank_multi.py around line 774) computes rule 1 and rule 3 over every action_owner_issues row. Nothing restricts them to questions that name no tracker, even though the rule's label says "when no tracker is named".
- questions() picks one wording per question with rng.choice from the pair (writer 1's and writer 2's template). So the test's roughly 8-9 action-item questions come from only 2 templates.

Development numbers, recomputed from dev_v9/v11/v10/v12.json against each set's questions.jsonl, counting a question as tracker-free when it contains neither "linear" nor "jira":
- Every dev set except mdplan_w3 and mdrep_w3 has 0 tracker-free action questions.
- On those sets v11-v9 on action items is 0.000, except +0.062 on mdtrain and +0.037 on mdblind. Those come from the listing side effect, not from the ticket rule.
- The whole gain comes from writer 3's template: mdplan_w3 +0.438 and mdrep_w3 +0.333.
- On those 17 tracker-free questions v9 already scored 1.0 on 10. The net gain is 6.5/17, about 0.38 per tracker-free question.
- v9's errors cluster on a few owners: Jordan Lee 4 times, Jordan Patel twice, Evan Park once.

What this means for the threshold:
- If only one of the two templates names no tracker, about half the questions, the expected gain is about 0.19. That is below +0.25, so a working rule would probably fail.
- If both templates name a tracker, the rule cannot reach +0.25.
- Rule 1's verdict therefore depends mainly on the sealed writers' choice of whether to name a tool, which the pre-registration itself says is unknown.

What the pre-registration does and does not cover:
- It says only "If few questions name no tracker, rule 1 has little to measure. How many ... will be reported." It does not say what that count changes.
- It also says "Rules 1 and 2 decide". So an outcome where the writers named a tracker would be either a misleading fail or a reading made after seeing the results.

What I could not establish: no copy of the brief exists outside blind4, which I did not open. So I cannot rule out that both writers avoided naming a tracker, which is the most favourable case. Even then, the outcome stays sensitive to v9's owner-clustered baseline.

The fix can be made before freezing without unblinding:
- Define "tracker-free" mechanically, for example no "linear" or "jira" in the question, ignoring case.
- Compute rules 1 and 3 on that subset.
- Declare a minimum count below which rule 1 is reported as "not measurable".

Not fixing it could flip or invalidate rule 1's verdict, so it matters for the test.

findings.title: The expected answers count only Linear items, yet the rule and the brief allow Jira; the Jira claim is true on earlier sets, but nothing says how a collision on the test set will be scored
findings.evidence:
No path for leakage found:
- ask_plans passes only q['question'] to plans.answer.
- v11's lessons differ from v9's only in weights, trained_on and tickets; I diffed the JSON, and the sha256 values match the pre-registration.
- No mdtick folder exists yet, and no test form caches exist under plan9/forms.

The expected answers come from by_person, which questions() builds from `lin` (Linear documents only). This applies to action_owner_issues, person_count and person_first.

I checked the pre-registration's claim on all nine earlier banks (mdtrain, mdtrainv9, mdtest, mdfresh, mdwords, mdblind, mdllm, mdplan, mdrep):
- People checked: action owners (pieces[0]); for person questions, the names in the question plus the assignee of each expected key.
- None has an assignee_of link to a Jira entity. The claim is TRUE.

The near-misses show it could still happen on a new draw:
- Some people not asked about do have Jira assignments: mdtrain Liam Chen (INT-4829), mdfresh Priya Nair (SUP-481516), mdblind Diego Martinez (SUP-901337).
- One owner who was asked about, Priya Shah in mdfresh, is reporter_of a Jira ticket (SUP-712345).

If it does happen, v11's list would include the Jira key and own_score would give F1 < 1 to an answer that is arguably right. That lowers rule 1, and re-scoring afterwards would be post hoc.

The selection rule's 'invalid wording' check (placeholders and length, per FACTBANK_GENERAL_PREREGISTRATION.md) does not catch a template that says 'Jira tickets' when the expected answer is Linear keys. The brief named no tracker, so a writer may well have written 'Jira'. Every arm would then fail those questions.
findings.fix:
Pre-declare now:
- How tracker-free 'ticket' questions are scored when the person has Jira items assigned: for example, excluded from rules 1-3 and reported separately, or scored against Linear plus Jira.
- How a template that names Jira (or another wrong tool) is treated when the expected answer is Linear-only: for example, excluded from rule 1 and reported.

verdict.reason:
I could not confirm the finding as a protocol defect, and its second half is refuted by a run.

**The mechanism is real, but the protocol already settles it.**
- Expected answers are built from Linear documents only (`questions()` uses `lin`).
- v11 treats "ticket" as Linear plus Jira (`in_system`, `TICKET_SYSTEMS`).
- Lists are scored by F1, so a collision would cost v11 some precision.
- The claim that nothing says how this is scored is wrong. The pre-registration says (line 76) that "the test's expected answers count only Linear issues". It commits to checking and reporting whether anyone asked about has Jira tickets (lines 76–78 and 137), and the measure is "as before", from frozen code. So scoring is fixed (Linear-only F1, then reported), and nothing allows re-scoring afterwards.
- The bias runs against v11, which is the conservative direction. v9 also has no system filter when it follows assignee_of, so a collision would lower v9's score too whenever v9 finds the owner's tickets.

**A collision is unlikely.** I re-ran the earlier-set check:
- Across the 9 banks, no person asked about has a Jira assignment.
- 5 of the 8 distinct sets (mdtest, mdwords, mdllm, mdplan, mdrep) contain no Jira documents at all. The other three have 2–6.
- Jira documents only enter through ticket units, which `fresh()` adds after action and PR units under the 50-document cap.
- One collision would move the action-item share by about 0.025 at most.

**"Every arm would then fail" a template that names Jira is refuted.** I took the earlier sets' (mdplan, mdrep, mdtest, mdllm, mdwords) action-item and person questions and replaced "Linear" with "Jira". Scored against the Linear-only expected answers:

| questions (n) | v11 | v9 |
|---|---|---|
| action items (42) | 0.988 | 0.697 |
| person_count (40) | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| person_first (37) | 0.865 | 0.865 |

These are the same as the tracker-free versions, apart from v9's action-item score. The reason: check 2 is skipped when no plan reaches a Jira item, so the arms still answer with the owner's Linear keys.

The pre-registration also already says that questions naming a tracker stay in rule 1, and that the count naming none will be reported (lines 131–132).

I did not open blind4, did not draw the test set and did not modify any repository file. My scripts are in scratchpad/audit_ticket_jira/ (chk.py, jira_named.py).

findings.title: Development description: no seen data is hidden, but the action-item gain comes from one wording the rule was built on; the 'Why' counts come from single-writer reruns; v12's new-words gain is right for the wrong reason
findings.evidence:
The development table is accurate: every cell recomputes exactly from dev_v9/v11/v10/v12.json. The mapping is mdtrain, mdtrainv9, mdtest, mdfresh, mdwords, mdblind, mdllm, mdplan, mdrep, then mdplan_w3 and mdrep_w3 for the two plain-words rows.

The two bold rows are one wording. Both mdplan_w3 and mdrep_w3 use the identical template 'Whoever got the "…" to-do in the "…" meeting, can you list the ticket IDs that are assigned to them?'. All 7 fixed questions use it, and the rule was designed around it. They are fits to seen data, not two confirmations.

The 'Why' counts are not from the tests as drawn:
- 'v9 got 4 of 8 such questions wrong on the first test and 3 of 9 on the replication' comes from the writer-3-only reruns, and the pre-registration does not say so (FACTBANK_PLAN_REPLICATION.md does).
- On the tests as drawn, both action templates say 'Linear', and v9 lost no action item to this cause. mdplan's 0.938 is the date-ordering question; mdrep scores 1.000.

One gain is not right for the right reason:
- v12's new-words gain over v10 (0.947 to 0.965) is a single question, ticket_link-status-041 ('ENG-73005 references another ticket. How far along is that one?').
- It goes from 0 to 1 while its right-for-the-right-reason score stays 0.0.
- The 'What changed' list does not mention it.

In-sample gains: 3 of the 4 'side effect' questions are mdtrainv9 142-144, which are one action item in three wordings. They sit inside v11's own training set.
findings.fix:
Add to the Development section:
- The two bold rows are one writer's one template, the one the rule was built to fix.
- The 4/8 and 3/9 counts come from the writer-3-only reruns.
- The mdwords v10 to v12 change is right by coincidence.
- The training 'side effect' gains are on v11's own training questions.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute each claim and could not. Every factual part of the finding checks out against the dev files and question sets.

1. **The table is accurate.** Every cell recomputes from dev_v9/v11/v10/v12.json. The two plain-words rows are mdplan_w3 and mdrep_w3.

2. **The two bold rows are one wording.** All 17 action-item questions in mdplan_w3 and mdrep_w3 use the same writer-3 template: 'Whoever got the "…" to-do in the "…" meeting, can you list the ticket IDs that are assigned to them?'. The 7 questions v11 fixes are mdplan_w3 021/024/041/042 and mdrep_w3 022/029/037, and all are in that template. Under v9 they all went to fireflies. Under v11 they go to assignee_of [ticket].

3. **The 'Why' counts come from the writer-3 reruns.**
   - As drawn, every mdplan and mdrep action item says 'Linear' (writers 1 and 2), and v9 plans assignee_of [linear] on all of them.
   - On mdplan as drawn, v9 scores 7.5/8 = 0.938 on action items. The one miss is 021, the date-ordering question, which every version gets wrong. On mdrep as drawn it scores 9/9.
   - So the 4/8 and 3/9 come only from the writer-3-only reruns, which FACTBANK_PLAN_RESULTS.md and FACTBANK_PLAN_REPLICATION.md list as 'after the run; information only'.
   - The pre-registration's 'The planner test and its replication found… on the first test' does not say so. The quoted template and the row labels only hint at it.

4. **v12's new-words gain is right by coincidence.**
   - The whole mdwords v10→v12 change (0.947→0.965) is one question, ticket_link-status-041. It goes from 0 to 1 while its right-for-the-right-reason score stays 0. That is why both versions have reason 0.93.
   - v12's plan reads the status of ENG-73005 itself ('[ticket] → status'), not the linked ENG-61234. It is right only because both are 'In Progress'.
   - 'What changed' does not mention this.

5. **The side-effect gains are mostly one training item.** They are mdtrain 035, mdtrainv9 142/143/144 and mdblind 028. mdtrainv9 142–144 are one action item ('Draft step-by-step runbook… emergency key rotation') in three wordings, inside the 201 training questions v11 was re-weighted on. The doc does say 'in training', but not that three of the four are the same item.

These are real gaps in how the development section describes things, though closer to low than medium severity. The section already says all its sets were seen.

**They do not matter for the test.**
- The rules are scored on a new, sealed set by new writers, and none of these points changes a rule, a number or a verdict.
- Rule 4 (a guard) passes without the coincidental question. v12 is level with or above v10 on every earlier held-out set. v11 minus v9 averages about −0.002 across the seven sets, inside the 0.01 margin.
- The fixes are wording changes to a descriptive section, so they do not affect the test's fairness.

findings.title: Rule 7 cannot fail and is not marked as known; rule 3 is not independent of rule 1
findings.evidence:
Rule 7:
- In development, v11 and v12 both score 1.000 on the 48 first training questions.
- v4 scores 0.927 there (measure() on the stored factbank_v4.jsonl), so the rule needs at least 0.897.
- All of these are fixed data and deterministic, so rule 7 cannot fail.
- The pre-registration marks only rule 4 as 'known from development' (7-set mean: v11-v9 = -0.002, v12-v10 = +0.003).

Rule 5's reference value is also fixed: v11 and v12 both score 1.000 on the 201 training questions, so the rule reduces to 'test >= 0.85'.

Rule 3:
- In every development set, the per-question changes from v10 to v12 on action items are identical to those from v9 to v11 (same question ids, same scores).
- The model's form never changed an action-item answer, so rule 3 will move with rule 1 and adds no independent evidence.

Rules that can genuinely fail: rule 2 (a margin of -0.03 allows one lost question in about 41; two fail), rule 5 against the test set, and rule 6.
findings.fix: Mark rule 7, and rule 5's reference value, as known from development, as is already done for rule 4, or drop rule 7. Note that rule 3 is expected to follow rule 1 and is not a separate confirmation.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute the finding but its main factual claims hold.

Rule 7 cannot fail:
- I ran measure() on mdtrain (the first 48 training questions). v4 scores 0.927 from the stored factbank_v4.jsonl, so the threshold is 0.897.
- dev_v11.json and dev_v12.json both score mdtrain at 1.000.
- The run script recomputes v11 and v12 on mdtrain from the frozen plan_lessons_v11.json. v12 reads its forms from the cached plan9/forms/form_mdtrain.jsonl, which has 48 lines for the 48 questions, so it needs no new model calls. Everything is fixed data.
- ticket_test's rule 7 compares t["v11"] and t["v12"] against t["v4"] on exactly this set. It is certain to pass.
- The draft marks only rule 4 as "known from development, so it is a guard rather than a test". Rule 7 has no such note.

Rule 3 tracks rule 1, empirically:
- Across all 15 development sets (mdtrain, mdtrainv9, mdtest, mdfresh, mdwords, mdblind, mdllm, mdplan and its three writers, mdrep and its three writers), v9 and v10 give identical per-question scores on action_owner_issues, and so do v11 and v12.
- So the per-question changes from v10 to v12 equal those from v9 to v11 everywhere (for example +0.438 on mdplan_w3 and +0.333 on mdrep_w3).

Where the finding goes too far:
- Rule 3's link to rule 1 is not guaranteed by the code. In plans.answer, the form is used only when the lessons are unsure (`asked = asked or form["kind"]`, plus its fields), so a new test wording could still let the form change an action-item answer. Rule 3 is very likely, not certain, to follow rule 1.
- The draft already says "Rules 1 and 2 decide whether the ticket rule works". It labels rule 3 "the same with the small model's form", so it does not present rule 3 as independent evidence.
- Rule 5's reference value (1.000 on the 201 questions) being known is ordinary. Rule 5 can still fail against the test set.
- The same unmarked rule 7 appeared in FACTBANK_PLAN_PREREGISTRATION.md, so this carries on an earlier convention.

Net: the finding is real but minor, and only about disclosure. Fixing it changes no test number and no verdict, because rule 7 truly passes and rules 1 and 2 decide the outcome. It does not affect fairness either; it only affects how plainly the draft labels a guard.

findings.title: The brief supplied the exact word the rule keys on
findings.evidence:
The rule matches TICKET_WORD = \b(?:tickets?|issues?)\b.

The pre-registration says 'This brief says "ticket" and "pull request" only' and 'Earlier briefs said "Linear issue", and writers copied it.'

By its own observation, the writers are likely to copy 'ticket', the exact token the rule matches. So the test cannot show whether tracker-free questions using other nouns (to-do, task, work item, bug, what's on their plate) are handled. 'The writers chose for themselves' covers naming a tool, not the noun.
findings.fix: State this limitation in the pre-registration. Report how many action-item wordings contain the trigger word and how many use another noun.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute the finding, so it stands. Each claim checks out against the code and data.

**What the code and data show:**
- **The rule keys on one word.** `TICKET_WORD` in plans.py:46 is `\b(?:tickets?|issues?)\b`, and `systems_named` adds the "ticket" system only when that regex matches (plans.py:335).
- **The pre-registration names the word.** It says "This brief says 'ticket' and 'pull request' only". It also says "Earlier briefs said 'Linear issue', and writers copied it".
- **Development never saw another noun.** I checked every action-item question (kind `action_owner_issues`) in all 15 development sets, from mdtrain through mdrep_w3. All of them contain the trigger word. The only tracker-free wording, from the plain-words writer (mdplan_w3 and mdrep_w3), says "ticket IDs".

**A concrete check.** I took the mdplan_w3 action items and changed only the noun "ticket IDs", answering each version with v9 lessons and with v11 lessons. The v11 lessons file is scratchpad/tick/plan_lessons_v11.json.

| noun | v9 | v11 |
|---|---|---|
| "ticket IDs" | 0.5 | 0.938 |
| "task IDs", "work item IDs", "bug IDs", "to-do IDs", "tracker keys" | 0.5 | 0.5 |

With the other nouns, `systems_named` returns only `['fireflies']` and v11 gains nothing. So the rule helps only with the word the brief gave the writers.

**What the pre-registration misses:**
- It does not state this limitation.
- It promises to report how many action items name no tracker, but not how many contain the trigger word versus another noun.
- `ticket_test` in factbank_multi.py does not compute that count either.
- The heading of rule 1, "answers action items when no tracker is named", claims more than the test can show if the writers copied "ticket".

**Why it does not change the test:**
- No number or verdict changes.
- The tilt toward the rule comes from the brief, which was already sent, and the wordings are already sealed. Adding the disclosure cannot undo that.
- The project's title claim is "a ticket means Linear or Jira", and the test fits that scope.
- The trigger-word count is mechanical. It can be computed and reported after the test without any room for choice, though adding the limitation and the count before freezing would be cleaner.

I did not open blind4, and I did not modify any repository file. My check script is scratchpad/refute_noun.py.

findings.title: The frozen-code entry points at the draft commit
findings.evidence:
The Frozen table says 'code | the commit that adds this document'. git log --diff-filter=A shows the document was added by bbf5e1b ('work in progress, under review').

The banner says the design is frozen only by the commit that removes the draft line. If the review changes code, the stated frozen commit is the code from before the review.
findings.fix: Change the entry to 'the commit that removes the draft line', and record that commit's hash in the results.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute this. The contradiction is in the text and the git history confirms it. The working tree is clean, and HEAD is bbf5e1b ("A ticket means Linear or Jira (v11, v12): work in progress, under review"). That commit adds cie/docs/FACTBANK_TICKET_PREREGISTRATION.md (git log --diff-filter=A) along with the code changes (plans.py +47, factbank_multi.py +64, tests, lessons, run script). The document it adds still has line 3: "Draft, under review: the design is frozen only by the commit that removes this line." The Frozen table (line 144) says "code | the commit that adds this document", which can only mean bbf5e1b, the draft commit. So the document names two different commits as the frozen code. If the review changes any code before the draft line is removed, the table points to pre-review code. Nothing else pins the code: run_ticket.sh records no commit and no code hash.

The last cycle shows the same thing happening for real. FACTBANK_PLAN_PREREGISTRATION.md carries the identical wording. It was added in the work-in-progress commit e136b3c, but the freeze commit 7017046 then changed plans.py (94 lines) and factbank_multi.py (37 lines). Read literally, that document's "commit that adds this document" pointed at code that was not the frozen code. FACTBANK_PLAN_RESULTS.md settled it by recording "The design was frozen at commit 7017046".

This is a wording problem in the record and does not affect the test. It changes no number and no rule verdict. The blinding and the test set are unaffected, because the run uses whatever code is checked out when it starts. The banner already says what actually freezes the design, and the earlier results write-up shows the actual freeze commit gets recorded. The suggested fix (say "the commit that removes the draft line" and record its hash in the results) is still worth making for an accurate record.
